**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Article II grant satisfies the preferred position on every material term of the LICENSE rule:

- **Affiliates:** Section 2.2(a) gives us the right to sublicense Array Patents and Array Know-How to our Affiliates without consent (better than the fallback's "on written notice"); Section 2.1(b) permits Affiliate sublicensing of the Manufacturing licence.
- **Contractors:** Section 2.1(b) expressly allows extension to Third Party manufacturers Manufacturing on our behalf, and the Section 1.57 "Subcontractor" definition contemplates our subcontracting of Agreement activities.
- **Not revocable at will:** Array may terminate only for uncured material breach (90 days; 60 for payment) or insolvency under Sections 13.3–13.4. On expiry, Section 13.1 converts our licences to "non-exclusive, fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights."
- **Successor transfer:** Section 18.9 permits assignment without consent to an acquirer of substantially all of our business or assets, and the Agreement inures to successors and permitted assigns.

Noted but not flagged (minor sub-elements): Array's prior written consent for Third Party Sublicensees/distributors, and consent — not to be unreasonably withheld — for intra-group assignment. Both are customary in pharma collaborations and do not fail the fallback. The Section 2.6 Grant-Back runs from us to Array but is confined to Improvements and our Joint IP interest and is expressly subject to our exclusive rights, so it does not erode the inbound grant.
